text:
maya: thinking out loud — what if we use very small, appendable 'mini-checkpoints' (delta blobs) next to safetensors bundles as an optional warmup path? goal: cut cold-start IO / verification time for common hot paths without requiring full checkpoint hotload.

joel: curious — how do you imagine the loader/runtime boundary? atomic apply? validation? sounds risky if not well-specified.

maya: yep atomicity is the main worry. rough idea: store the primary safetensors as usual + an optional .mini file per shard. mini contains only layers that change often (layernorm/kv slices/etc) and a tiny header with checksum + base-commit id. loader reads main header first, then decides whether to fetch/apply mini. manifest stub: 
```
mini_v1: true
mini_files:
  - shard-000.mini: {commit: "abc123", checksum: "sha256:...", size: 48MB}
  - shard-001.mini: {...}
```

if commit mismatch -> treat mini as incompatible.

sam: what about eviction/backpressure? applying a .mini could temporarily spike mem while merging overlay -> risk OOM on busy hosts. also extra IO ops per request if we do on-demand.

rachel: agree. gating policy idea: only apply mini when request QPS < threshold OR available_gpu_mem > X% + a safe margin. metrics to track: apply_time, rollback_time, failed_applies, mini_hit_ratio.

linh: alternative: stream-apply mini lazily as small patches into an ephemeral slab (LRU) so we don't copy whole shard. patch format must be position+len+payload. eviction would just drop patches, restoring to base checkpoint semantics. downside: fragmentation and more complex K/V cache interactions.

joel: fallback semantics pls: if mini apply fails mid-apply, we must ensure loader falls back to base safely and doesn't leave partially-applied state visible to inference threads. how to coordinate with KV cache and active generation frames?

maya: plan: loader treats mini as advisory overlay. apply sequence pseudo: 
```
fetch mini -> verify checksum -> write to tmp overlay object -> atomically swap overlay pointer (loader uses versioned pointers) -> warmup hooks populate kvcache for overlay pages -> if failure, swap pointer back, delete tmp -> log and metric "mini_apply_failed"
```
so critical: pointer swap must be atomic w.r.t inference thread view. no in-place edits.

dev-bot: deploy-preview: mini-checkpoint-loader spike branch pushed to canary cluster (canaries: 3 nodes) :rocket:

sam: extra cost: manifest lookup per model load. can we piggyback on header fetch (single request) so we don't double roundtrip? also consider signed manifests (KMS) for enterprise.

rachel: backward compatibility: older runtimes should ignore mini fields. add a top-level field `mini_v1` and a graceful ignore path. rollout: loader will opt-in via flag `--enable-mini` for 2 weeks on canary.

linh: still worried about fragmentation if many tiny patches are applied. maybe quantify: spike alloc if we do copy-based apply vs patch-based. need microbench.

maya: agreed. proposed next steps: 2-week spike (loader + runtime pointer-swap + metrics) -> microbench: cold-start (no mini), mini-apply-time, OOM probability under synthetic load -> then RFC with API surface (manifest fields, overlay pointer semantics, metrics). volunteers?

joel: I'll take the loader atomicity + tests.

linh: I'll do the patch-format and eviction microbench.

rachel: I'll own the metrics/dashboard + rollout plan.

maya: awesome — I'll draft a short spike README and link a tiny gist with the manifest sketch, then we convert to RFC if spike is promising. moving to a doc after the spike sounds good. :+1:

maya: gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/mini-checkpoint-proto (WIP)
